units.name: SKS 300 "Kaiser"

tier.basis: Built at the Advanced Saxon Workshop, by the wiki's infobox. DevBlog #30 (September 2020) took the three mega mechs, the Kaiser among them, out of the Reserve and made them need an Advanced Barracks on top of an Advanced Workshop. Change Log #04 later dropped the barracks need for campaign and challenge maps only, so skirmish and multiplayer still ask for both, and no later post read changes that. Both advanced buildings together are the tier map's t3 gate.

cost_band.basis: DevBlog #43 (December 2021) set the iron and oil price that the wiki's infobox has shown since January 2022, and no later post read changes it. Counted as iron plus three times the oil, it lands a little above the high threshold and well short of very high: about half again what the anchor line mechs such as the Wotan cost, and the dearest of the mega mechs. Its population cost, among the largest in the game, uses up the cap rather than paying a price, so it is left out.

mobility.notes: Walks on four legs at a little under half the pace of the rifle squads, the game's speed reference, and its own page ranks it among the slowest units of all, easy to flank and outpace. Iron Harvest has no tanks: it is somewhat slower than the Wotan, Saxony's line mech, keeps about the Tur's pace and lags behind the Gulyay-Gorod, the other mega mechs. Handling stays pivot, the many-legs default: it is far too big for the small walkers' strafe, and no source gives another reason to change it. From its first veterancy rank it can entrench, and then it can neither walk nor turn (deploy-anchor). Like the other heaviest mechs it walks straight through brick and stone buildings and flattens cover, sandbags and wire underfoot: game-wide terrain breaking, not the crush trait.

body.notes: A boxy hull plated like a bunker and standing on four legs; the wiki's Saxony page says Saxon mechs often look like conventional tanks on spider or crab legs. The cannon sits on the roof in an armoured housing of its own that looks like a turret but is locked facing forward, so the whole mech turns to aim it, and a machine gun in a ball mount guards each of its four sides. Spider frame, by the Iron Harvest notes for a walker on many legs whose main gun is fixed: the gun locked forward shows in the cannon's body-aim mount, and the tank-like hull only in these notes (see uncertain and fit_notes). Entrenching lifts the cannon housing to bare rocket batteries at the front and on both flanks; the body plan stays the same. Huge: KING Art presented it with the Tur as two of the biggest mechs in the game, and giant mechs are huge in our size examples, although its own page calls it far more compact than the Tur (see uncertain).

armour.notes: Step 1 of the armour-class steps reads the infobox's Heavy as heavy through the armour map; the registry note and check A make the mega mechs super-heavy, and it is huge and tier 3. Its health tops that of every other mega mech and of the Samson, and its page ranks only the Icarus as tougher, shrugging off almost everything short of massed artillery. By the Armor page, heavy armour all but ignores light weapons, so only field cannons and anti-mech weapons do it real harm. Directional: hits on its rear do about twice the damage (Armor page), and its own page says it suffers more from behind, where neither the cannon nor the rockets can answer. Veterancy raises its health by about a third and then by half, and repair at the base is game-wide; neither changes the class.

sensors.notes: No source gives sight figures for Iron Harvest units (the registry's sight reference), so the band is the medium proposal. No source gives it radar, a detector or stealth.

armament.name: Main Cannon
armament.summary: A big gun in the forward-locked roof housing: it fires only where the hull points, so the mech turns to bring it to bear. One heavy shell at a time with a long pause between shots, reaching about three quarters further than the reference rifle. By the infobox it hits the game's Light armour class hardest, Medium a little less and Heavy as hard as infantry, while buildings take half that. Each shell bursts over a small area, but the blast is far weaker than the Tur's, so on its own the gun deals poorly with groups of soft targets. The wiki calls it the Kaiser's main anti-armour firepower and says it lets the mech beat any other mech one on one. While entrenched it can only cover a narrow arc ahead.

armament.name: Side Machine Gun
armament.summary: Four heavy machine guns in ball mounts, one on each side of the hull: between them they watch every direction, and they keep shooting while the mech walks. Each fires long bursts with short pauses and reaches a little less far than the reference rifle. The infobox shows them doing little to any armour and next to nothing to heavy armour or buildings, so they are for infantry and light mechs.

armament.name: Rockets
armament.summary: Three six-tube batteries, one at the front and one on each flank, that the rising cannon housing bares when the Kaiser entrenches; none faces the rear. While it stays dug in, each attack order fires them beside the cannon and machine guns: salvos of fifteen small rockets every few seconds, each rocket bursting over an area. By the infobox they hit infantry (the game's Unarmored class, by the Armor page) about three times as hard as the Light and Medium classes and the Heavy class least, with some harm to buildings. They reach about two fifths further than the reference rifle but not as far as the cannon, and the wiki counts their short reach among its faults.

crew.notes: No player seats: RTS units are ordered, not driven, and no page read names a crew, so the walker class makes it a crewed machine. Driver-gunner: once it has entrenched, its rocket batteries, on mounts of their own at the front and flanks of the hull, fire beside the forward cannon, which keeps shooting into its narrow arc (the Kaiser page says they add firepower). By decision 2A the driver walks the mech, aims the cannon by turning the body and fires the side machine guns, since no source says those fire at the same moment as the cannon; the gunner fires the rockets, which pass to the driver when no gunner is aboard. It has no passenger seats.

abilities.name: Entrench
abilities.summary: Opens once the Kaiser reaches its first veterancy rank (the wiki; patch 0.11.2 let the mega mechs rank up a little faster). The mech plants itself and can neither walk nor turn, and the cannon housing rises to bare the rocket batteries, the entrenched mode's Rockets (armament/2). Dug in, the cannon covers only a narrow arc ahead. Planting takes a moment in which it is exposed, and a planted Kaiser suffers even more from field cannons and artillery. No source gives a cooldown, how long the change takes or how it packs up again.

modes.name: Entrenched
modes.summary: Dug in: it cannot move or turn. The raised cannon housing bares the Rockets (armament/2), batteries that fire only in this mode, to the front and both flanks but not behind; the cannon keeps firing, but only into a narrow arc ahead. Nothing read says the side machine guns fall silent or that its armour changes. The wiki says field cannons and artillery hurt it most in this state.

on_death.notes: Like any destroyed mech it leaves a wreck, which nearly any infantry squad can strip, the way it collects a resource stockpile, for a little iron and oil, the same small haul whatever mech it was (DevBlog #24; Recycling Wrecks page); since Change Log #04 allies get the haul too. Another mech or exosuit stepping on the wreck, an explosion such as an artillery strike, or a death too close to a live mech wipes it out first, and the wreck gives infantry no cover. No source says its destruction harms anything nearby.

strengths.why: Only the Icarus is tougher: its health tops every other mega mech's and the Samson's, and its heavy plating shrugs off small arms, so it can head a formation and soak fire while little but massed artillery wears it down.
Its long-reaching main cannon hits every armour class hard, so it can duel and destroy any other mech one on one, the other mega mechs included.
Machine guns at the front, the back and both flanks keep infantry off it whichever way they come, and they fire while it walks.
Once veteran it can entrench to open rocket batteries that add salvos to its front and both flanks, and a supported pair of dug-in Kaisers makes a line that enemies can hardly break.
As one of the largest mechs it walks straight through brick and stone buildings that stop smaller mechs and over cover, sandbags and wire, so few obstacles block its path.

weaknesses.why: It ranks among the game's slowest units: it cannot chase, and lighter units outmanoeuvre it, flank it and keep out of its reach.
The cannon is locked facing forward, so a target on its flank or behind it is safe from its anti-armour gun until the slow mech turns.
Hits from behind do about double damage, and neither its cannon nor its rockets can fire to the rear, leaving only the rear machine gun to answer there.
Dug in, it cannot walk or turn and its cannon covers only a narrow arc ahead; planting leaves it briefly exposed, and field cannons and artillery hurt it even more while it is planted.
The cannon reloads slowly and its blast is weak, so until its machine guns or rockets are in reach it handles soft targets and groups of light units poorly, worse than the Tur or the Gulyay-Gorod do.
The priciest Saxon unit to build, and its heavy population cost keeps the number in the field small.

countered_by.why: Artillery is the bane of the slow heavy mechs (Unit page), and massed artillery is what the Kaiser page says wears it down, all the more once it digs in and can no longer step out of the fire.

Heavy armour is hurt in earnest only by field cannons and by mechs carrying anti-mech guns (Armor page), and the Kaiser page names enough well-placed field cannons among its main dangers, above all against a planted Kaiser.
Named on the Kaiser page: field cannons in numbers and in good positions grind it down, above all while it is entrenched.
Agile units at rifle-squad pace or faster, more than twice its speed, slip round to its flanks and rear, where the cannon cannot follow and hits do about double, and can lead it on a chase.

counters.why: Its cannon can duel and kill any other mech one on one, the other mega mechs included, and its machine guns also tear into light mechs.
Its four machine guns mow down infantry closing in from any side, even while it walks, and once it digs in its rockets add bursts that hit soldiers hardest.

combos.why: The Kaiser page advises fielding at least two together, and a supported pair dug in makes a nearly unbreakable line, the core of the Saxony page's defensive formation.
It soaks the fire while anti-armour mechs add the damage: its page wants mech destroyers beside it on the attack and lists the Wotan among the Saxon support a defensive pair of Kaisers wants.
The Wotan page says the fragile Wotan does well behind a Kaiser that takes the hits while the Wotans add firepower.
The Kaiser page pairs it with artillery when it goes on the attack, and the Saxony page's formation can add the long-range Erlkönig.
Anti-infantry backup covers its gaps on the attack (Kaiser page), and the Grimbart, an anti-infantry mech, is among the support that its page and the Saxony page's formation give a pair of Kaisers.

units.memorable: Saxony's walking fortress, a bunker on four legs: a forward-locked cannon that out-duels any mech, a machine gun on every side and, once veteran, rockets bared by digging in.
units.as_player: A late, costly walking fortress that leads the push. Left mouse fires the forward-locked cannon, a slow, heavy shot that hurts any armour, so you aim by turning the whole lumbering mech; right mouse sweeps the side machine guns over infantry on any side, even on the move. Once you rank up, the deploy key digs you in: you cannot move or turn and the cannon covers only a narrow cone, while a gunner, or you alone, fires the rockets on your front and flanks. Guard your back, where hits do double.

sources.title: SKS 300 "Kaiser", Iron Harvest Wiki
sources.version: Last edited 10 January 2022 (price from DevBlog #43); weapon figures entered April 2020, health September 2020, speed May 2021 (page history)
sources.note: Read through the wiki's API, with its page history; marked beta. The infobox gives health, armour class Heavy, speed, price and population, and three weapon slots, the Main Cannon, the Side Machine Gun and the Entrench rockets (that slot marked as an ability), with reach, burst, pause, damage per armour class and blast. The prose gives the forward-locked cannon, the four ball-mounted guns, Entrench as the veteran ability, the rear weakness and the matchups. Its italic opening line, Lore box, unit type and Pros and Cons are the wiki's own words, which the roles rules do not read as official text.

sources.title: Armor, Iron Harvest Wiki
sources.note: The game's four unit armour classes, heavy armour being hurt in earnest only by field cannons and anti-mech weapons, and the weak rear spots of many mechs, where damage is doubled.

sources.title: Iron Harvest DevBlog #24 - April 2020, KING Art Games
sources.note: Brings in the Kaiser among the beta's new units, under the heading Saxony Gunfort: a top-end mech with a cannon and several machine guns that can deploy so that its rocket launchers fire. The same post makes the wrecks of destroyed mechs harvestable, and its patch notes let rockets, like grenades and artillery shells, hurt targets some way from the centre of the blast. A beta-era post, so no figure rests on it; the wiki adds that the deploy comes with the first veterancy rank.

sources.title: Iron Harvest DevBlog #30 - September 2020, KING Art Games
sources.note: From this patch the three mega mechs, the Kaiser among them, can be built only once the player has an Advanced Workshop as well as an Advanced Barracks, and no reserve offers them any more.

sources.title: Iron Harvest DevBlog #43 - December 2021, KING Art Games
sources.note: The mech cost rebalance labels the unit Kaiser (Mega Mech), the newest bracketed label, and sets its price in iron and oil, which the wiki's infobox matches; no later post read, up to DevBlog #47, changes it.

uncertain.note: Step 1 finds no role: the newest bracketed label, Mega Mech (DevBlog #43), names none, and neither does DevBlog #24's older Saxony Gunfort heading. No official text read says what it is strong against, and the registry finds no bonus in the game data, so step 4 finds nothing and step 5 gives assault: very slow and super-heavy. The Lore box on its wiki page, which may copy the in-game Codex (the wiki shows the Codex only as a picture), calls it effective against both infantry and mechs; no readable source shows that line in the game, so it is read as the wiki's words, like its italic opening line. Read as official, step 4 would offer anti-infantry and anti-armour with no bonus to rank them, and the line names infantry first.

Anti-armour rests on the Kaiser page's prose calling the cannon its main anti-armour firepower, read as a label that names the weapon by its job (can_target step 3); without it the list would be anti-infantry alone, from the splash cannon and the side machine guns, small arms that do little to mechs. Siege is no candidate: the cannon reaches long but is aimed straight at targets in view, the rockets that entrenching adds reach only medium and are not lobbed, so the mode fails siege's deploy clause, and Entrench, a veteran button that not every copy has, gives nothing at step 2. The rockets count at step 3 as a secondary weapon although only a dug-in veteran fires them; they add only anti-infantry, through their splash, which the other weapons already give. The wiki's Cons call the cannon poor against soft targets, but they are the wiki's words, not official text, so they drop nothing.

The infobox names only the Advanced Saxon Workshop, and the Advanced Saxon Workshop page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Advanced_Saxon_Workshop) lists the Kaiser among the units it builds; the Advanced Barracks comes from DevBlog #30. Change Log #04 (https://kingart-games.com/article/92) removed that second building for campaign and challenge maps only and says multiplayer and skirmish keep it; no later post read changes it. Both pages read, not cited.

The Kaiser page's Cons still rank it second among the game's dearest units, a line written before DevBlog #43; at the current prices it tops the registry's price check list, ahead of the Tur, the Samson and the Gulyay-Gorod.

The infobox speed was entered on 23 May 2021 by an anonymous edit with no comment, in place of an April 2020 figure a little lower, and no KING Art post read from DevBlog #20 to #47 changes the Kaiser's speed. Either figure is under half the reference pace, so the band holds. The comparisons in mobility.notes use the infobox speeds on the SKS 156 "Wotan", PZM-24 "Tur" and SHM-70 "Gulay-Gorod" pages of the Iron Harvest Wiki (read, not cited).

Deploy-anchor stands for Entrench, which a Kaiser gains only at its first veterancy rank, so an unranked Kaiser cannot deploy. It is kept because the button and its mode are recorded, as on the Red Alert 2 deploy units; mobility traits have no stock-only rule like the one for sensor traits.

Walking through buildings and over cover rests on the Unit page (the heavy and mega mechs pass easily through brick and stone buildings), the Mech page (the biggest mechs trudge through large structures) and the Sandbags page (mechs flatten sandbags by stepping on them), all on the Iron Harvest Wiki, read, not cited; the Kaiser page itself says nothing of buildings.

Coded spider-frame by the Iron Harvest notes' reading for walkers on many legs (night decision of 27 October 2026), until a body tie-break for such walkers is settled at the rule-fix round after R4. In the opening check one coder chose spider-frame and the other casemate. By the casemate or hull-turret tie-break, a main gun locked forward in the hull makes a fixed-gun hull. But casemate is listed only for ground vehicles and hovercraft of medium or large size, so the Kaiser would break three of its rules, as the reconciled entry did before this note. The Saxony Empire page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Saxony_Empire, read, not cited) says Saxon mechs often look like conventional tanks on spider or crab legs. Multi-turret would fit only if the four ball-mounted guns, which the wiki calls machine gun turrets, counted as turrets; the note says they do not.

No source gives its footprint. KING Art's DevBlog #22 (https://kingart-games.com/article/74, read, not cited) introduced it with the Tur as two of the largest mechs in the game and called both huge; the game labels it a Mega Mech (DevBlog #43), and the wiki's Unit page calls the heavy and mega mechs the biggest mechs. Coded huge from the giant mechs of the size examples. Against that, the Kaiser page's trivia calls it much more compact than the Tur; large would follow only if it were judged no bigger than an assault mech.

The armour map alone gives heavy (infobox Heavy); super-heavy comes from the registry note on the mega mechs and from check A for a huge unit at tier 3. The health comparisons in armour.notes and strengths/0 use the infobox figures on the PZM-24 "Tur", SHM-70 "Gulay-Gorod" and ZR-25 "Samson" pages of the Iron Harvest Wiki (read, not cited).

The doubling comes from the Armor page; the Kaiser's own page says only that hits from behind do more. Versions of its page from May and June 2020 said it had no weak spot, until an August 2020 edit added the rear weakness, and no post read settles it, so directional follows the registry's rule for every mech.
No damage map: step 5 keeps the cannon default, armour-piercing, which the wiki's calling it the main anti-armour firepower also gives. If that wording did not count, its blast would give explosive.

Splash rests on the infobox's blast radius, which counts as saying the hit hurts an area. The Kaiser page calls the cannon's splash damage low and says it lacks the splash to handle infantry well, but it never calls the area tiny.

The infobox weapon figures (reach, damage, bursts and pauses) were entered in April 2020, during the backer beta, and no later KING Art post read changes the Kaiser's weapons, so they are read as current. The comparisons use the registry's reference rifle.
No source says how the shell travels; projectile is the cannon family's default. Hitscan for the side machine guns is likewise their family's default.

None of the three weapons lists air targets, the rockets included. The Kaiser page's Pros suggest, with a hedge, that it can even shoot at airships, but they name no weapon, and no other source says which Kaiser weapon reaches aircraft; the Gunship page's claim that every unit can attack it is too broad (registry). The SHM-70 "Gulay-Gorod" page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (read, not cited) says that mech's machine guns fire at flying units, which may hold for the Kaiser's guns too. Structures are listed from the infobox's building damage figures.

Limited-arc: each machine gun sits in a ball mount on one side of the hull, and no source says how far it turns (aim tie-break step 3). By that step the front gun alone would be fixed; the one entry takes the side guns' mount.

Only a Kaiser that has reached its first veterancy rank and dug in fires the batteries, so not every copy has them. They are coded as a secondary weapon of the entrenched mode, as the registry note on the infobox's ability slots now says for the Kaiser's Rockets, and as the slot rule says of a weapon that a mode adds while the main gun keeps firing. Acquired does not fit: it covers a weapon that a rank adds with no ability, and here the rank opens the Entrench button, which enters the mode. Their figures come from the infobox's third weapon slot, the one marked as an ability, entered in April 2020 with the other weapons' figures.

Limited-arc: one battery faces forward and one faces each flank, and the Kaiser page says neither the rockets nor the cannon can fire to the rear (aim tie-break step 3). By that step the front battery alone would be fixed; the one entry takes the flank batteries' mount, as for the side machine guns. The page's Abilities line has entrenching raise its damage output on every side, which is read as the batteries together with the rear machine gun.

Driver-gunner rests on the rockets alone, which fire only for a veteran Kaiser that has dug in. The crew rule leaves out weapons that a mode swaps in and weapons that an upgrade, a passenger or a kill adds, but not one that a mode adds while the main gun keeps firing, and the Kaiser page has the rockets add firepower while the cannon still covers its narrow arc. If a weapon reached only through a veteran button should not count, the proposal would stay solo. The side machine guns stay with the driver because no source says they fire at the same moment as the cannon (the page says only that they fire on the move and cover every side); if they do, they would go to the gunner too.

The unlock at the first rank rests on the Kaiser page's Weapons section and on the Veterancy page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Veterancy, read, not cited), which says the first rank opens each unit's veteran ability; the Tur and Gulay-Gorod pages say the same of their mega-mech abilities. DevBlog #24, from the backer beta, lists the deploy with the unit, apart from the veteran abilities it names, without saying when it opens. Patch 0.11.2 (https://kingart-games.com/article/83, read, not cited) let all three mega mechs reach veterancy a little faster.

The wreck rests on DevBlog #24, which made mech wrecks harvestable, and on the Recycling Wrecks page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Recycling_Wrecks, read, not cited), which says every destroyed mech leaves one and gives who can recycle it and what removes it; Change Log #04 (https://kingart-games.com/article/92, read, not cited) shares the haul with allies. The Kaiser page says nothing of its wreck.

Artillery also rests on the Unit page of the Iron Harvest Wiki (https://iron-harvest.fandom.com/wiki/Unit, read, not cited), which calls the heavy and mega mechs slow and open to artillery. Field cannons go under anti-armour because the same page says their direct-fire guns pierce even heavy mech armour from far off, while the Kaiser's own page names them beside artillery and once groups them with it. The agile units that kite it are read as units at least as fast as the rifle squads, since its page gives no speed and nearly every unit outpaces it. Whether aircraft beat it is left open, since no source says which of its weapons reach fliers; DevBlog #45 (https://kingart-games.com/article/121, read, not cited) says the game lists the Gunship as effective against heavy armour.

The Kaiser page says it can kill any other mech, and the infantry and carried weapons too, but its Cons call it vulnerable to field cannons and its prose has massed, well-placed field guns wear it down, so the weapon systems stay out of counters and field cannons sit in countered_by.

The Wotan, Erlkönig and Grimbart parts rest on the Saxony Empire page (its Great Wall formation: a pair of Kaisers backed by a Wotan or a Stiefmutter, a Grimbart, sometimes a field cannon, and at times the Erlkönig) and on the SKS 156 "Wotan" page (Wotans do well behind a Kaiser that soaks damage), both on the Iron Harvest Wiki, read, not cited. The Kaiser page itself links the Wotan and the Grimbart among the support a defensive pair wants, and on the attack wants it backed by artillery, by mech destroyers and by units that deal with infantry.

units.researched_by: batch r3, opening check (agents A and B, reconciled)

fit_notes.wanted: a fixed-gun hull for walkers, on many legs and at huge size
fit_notes.note: The main gun is locked forward in an armoured housing on the roof of a boxy, bunker-like hull on four legs. Spider frame (a body on several visible legs) fits the legs, but not the tank-like hull with its fixed gun, which shows only in the cannon's body-aim mount. Our casemate plan has that shape, but it is listed only for wheeled, tracked and hover vehicles of medium or large size.

atypical.note: It walks on four legs at a little under half the rifle squads' pace by its infobox speed, and our many-legs type starts at slow; the Tur and the Wotan, the other heavy Iron Harvest mechs compared in mobility.notes, are very slow too.
